definition: Ebullient means bubbling over with cheerful enthusiasm.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ebullient. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ebullient should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Ebullient as ever, the debate coach burst in waving the tournament bracket like a winning lottery ticket.
Lively is bright, wide-awake energy, but it is milder than ebullient — nothing is overflowing yet.
Manic goes further than ebullient — ebullient energy is joyful and welcome; manic energy has tipped past control into frenzy.

Exuberant is ebullient's nearest neighbor: overflowing energy and high spirits, visible from across a field. The shade of difference is the bubbling — ebullient keeps its boiling-over, spilling-onto-everyone quality, while exuberant can be athletic and wordless: a dog tearing joyful circles is exuberant without making a sound.

Irrepressible describes what happens when someone tries to hold the spirits down: they pop straight back up, however hard you press. It is about the resilience of a mood, not its volume. Ebullient is the volume — cheer boiling over onto everyone nearby, whether or not anyone has tried to squash it.
